{{Short description|Dutch mathematician (c. 1630–1691)}}

[[File:Ferguson_-_Labyrinthus_algebrae,_1667_-_883583.jpg|thumb|''Labyrinthus algebrae'' (1667)]]

'''Johan Jacob Ferguson''' was a [[17th-century]] [[Dutch people|Dutch]] [[mathematician]] who corresponded with [[Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz]].<ref name="Maanen">{{Cite journal|author=Jan A. van Maanen|title=Korrespondenten von G. W. Leibniz: 11. Johan Ferguson geb. um 1630 in Haag(?), gest. vor dem 24. November 1706, vermutlich am 6. Oktober 1691 in Amsterdem|journal=Studia Leibnitiana|volume=22|issue=2|year=1990|pages=203–216|jstor=40694153|language=de}}</ref>

== Life ==
He was born around 1630, probably in [[The Hague]], and died before 24 November 1706, probably on 6 October 1691 in [[Amsterdam]].<ref name="Maanen" />

In his 1667 book ''Labyrinthus algebrae'', written in low [[Dutch language|Dutch]],<ref name="Rees1819">{{cite book|author=Abraham Rees|title=The Cyclopaedia; Or, Universal Dictionary of Arts, Sciences and Literature|volume=1|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bD9RAAAAcAAJ&pg=PP674|year=1819|location=London|publisher=Longman, Hurst|page=674|chapter=Algebra}}</ref> he shows the solutions of [[Cubic Equation|cubic]] and [[biquadratic equation]]s using new methods.<ref name="Rigaud1841">{{cite book|editor=Stephen Jordan Rigaud|editor-link=Stephen Rigaud|title=Correspondence of Scientific Men of the Seventeenth Century|volume=2|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=sQ9UAAAAcAAJ&pg=PA515|year=1841|location=Oxford|publisher=The University Press|pages=515–|isbn=9780598562197}}</ref>
The book had a partial translation in Latin (lost) and was sent to [[Isaac Newton]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Giornale di fisica|volume=31|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=12ZCAQAAIAAJ|year=1990|location=Bologna|publisher=Società italiana di fisica|language=it|page=115}}</ref><ref name="TarozziVloten1989">{{cite book|author1=G. Tarozzi|author2=Monique van Vloten|title=Radici, significato, retaggio dell'opera newtoniana|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=L024AAAAIAAJ|year=1989|location=Bologna|publisher=Società italiana di fisica|language=it|page=371}}</ref>
